rationale: design-import-refactor: generic change landed in Pulp per owner decision 2026-10-04; Vellum inherits (see inheritance ledger); a data:image URI in any format but PNG never drew, and sprite strips held as encoded bytes decoded every paint and dropped frames past their encoded byte length. canvas-kernel: Canvas gains measure_image_from_data, a header-only intrinsic-size read appended after the existing virtuals; the base reads a PNG IHDR (IHDR chunk required, dimensions within 2^31 - 1), Skia uses a deferred image (orientation applied, matching its draw) and CoreGraphics reads ImageIO pixel-size properties. retained-ui-kernel: AssetManager::decode_data_uri_bytes returns a data URI payload whatever the image format, following RFC 2397: a payload marked ;base64 (case-insensitive) is percent-unescaped and then base64-decoded, any other payload is percent-decoded, and a malformed escape in a non-base64 payload yields no bytes. ImageView keeps those bytes, sizes them once per source through measure_image_from_data, and draws them through the content-keyed inline cache; undecodable bytes are tried once, logged, and paint a placeholder labelled with the media type. Knob and Fader sprite strips loaded from bytes hash them once (SpriteStrip::data_key) and draw through the keyed cache; once a canvas has measured the bytes as decodable (only a successful measure is recorded on the shared strip), every frame within the declared size draws, and raw RGBA bytes keep the byte-count bound. Backends without a cache or decoder draw as before. No design-import, Chromium, rendering, packaging, or source-authority boundary moves.
